description: MajiData is the national monitoring and georeferenced information system on water and sanitation services that the Water Act 2016 requires Kenya's regulator to keep. Version 1 (2009) held socio-economic data on the urban poor in all urban low-income areas; version 2 (2015) added the licensed and served areas of water service providers and sanitation infrastructure from Water Sector Trust Fund projects; version 3 (2023) added maps of small-scale service providers in all 47 counties and existing spatial data for the water distribution and sewer networks of the licensed providers, with an admin portal for updates and approvals. The Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB) produces it. Coverage is national for Kenya. Access is on request: the portal offers a form to ask for data, with no download or licence stated. Caveats: the system holds the network data that already existed, in the page's words, and nothing is openly downloadable. Simulation uses: utility distribution and sewer network layouts and service areas for network modelling, capacity planning and hazard exposure of urban water systems. Related records: none catalogued yet; WASREB's utility performance data are in data-wasreb-kenya-water-service-provider-performance.
